memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Count off seven sabbath years - seven times seven years - so that the
seven sabbath years amount to a period of forty-nine years. Then have the
trumpet sounded everywhere on the tenth day of the seventh month; on the
Day of Atonement sound the trumpet throughout your land'"
- Lev 25:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After forty-nine years came the great fiftieth year — the Jubilee. And
notice exactly when it was announced: on the Day of Atonement, the day
when the nation's sin was covered. The trumpet of freedom sounded on the
day of forgiveness.

That order is no accident. Freedom followed atonement. First sin was
dealt with, then liberty rang out across the land.

Dear reader, this is the very shape of the gospel. Our freedom is not
something we achieve by effort; it flows from atonement already made.
Because Christ has dealt with our sin, the trumpet of freedom can sound
over our lives.

Jesus stood up in the synagogue at Nazareth, opened the scroll of
Isaiah, and read: He has sent me to proclaim freedom for the prisoners
and to set the oppressed free, to proclaim the year of the Lord's favour
(Luke 4:18-19). That last phrase echoes Jubilee. Then He sat down and
said, today this scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.

The Jubilee that Israel kept every fifty years pointed forward to the
liberty Christ brings. Paul says it is for freedom that Christ has set us
free (Gal 5:1).

Whatever has held you captive — guilt, shame, a past you cannot undo —
the trumpet has sounded because atonement has been made.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I understand my freedom as flowing from Christ's atonement?
2. What still holds me captive that Christ has already freed me from?
3. How can I live today as someone who is truly free?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, thank You that on the day sin was atoned for, freedom was
proclaimed. Help me live in the liberty You bought for me on the cross.
Amen.
